newsitem.title: USA: Simpson jury's award met with quiet gratification.
newsitem.headline: Simpson jury's award met with quiet gratification.

text.p: While cheers and sobs of joy filled the courtroom when O.J. Simpson was blamed for the murders of his ex-wife and her friend, Monday's punitive damage award was met with quiet gratification.

Kim Goldman, sister of murder victim Ronald Goldman, who cried out "Oh, my God" after Simpson was found responsible for the deaths by the same jury last Tuesday, remained composed as she heard the award of $12.5 million to her brother's divorced parents.
Goldman's father, Fred Goldman, who had wept openly in court at the verdict, simply sighed as he shook his head and stared at the floor on hearing Monday's decision.

The six-man, six-woman jury last week pinned responsibility for the June 12, 1994 killings on Simpson, awarding $8.5 million in compensatory damages to Ronald Goldman's heirs. On Monday they added another $25 million in punitive damages, to be split evenly between the plaintiffs.
In October 1995, a criminal court jury found Simpson innocent of the murders but the victims' families pressed ahead with a wrongful death lawsuit.
The punitive damage award was greeted by a hushed courtroom.

Nicole Brown Simpson's family members -- including her mother and father, Juditha and Louis, and sisters Denise, Tanya and Dominique -- remained almost stoic as they heard the award. Denise offered only a small nod.
Outside the courthouse, police on horseback stood by in anticipation of the same unruly throng that surrounded the building after the first verdict, but instead found only a small crowd of onlookers.
Across the street at a hotel, family members expressed relief that their long ordeal was finally over.
"This has taken 2-1/2 years out of all our lives and this is going to affect us for the rest of our lives," Kim Goldman said as she fought back tears.

"I'll be glad when all the cameras are gone and we can sort of sit and look at our family and be proud of what we've done and be able to go to the cemetary as a family and tell Ron that we did it," she added.
Fred Goldman said Monday's damage award was not significant in comparison to the verdict finding Simpson liable for the killings.
"The jury's decision of last Tuesday was the only decision that was important to us," he said. "Having the killer of my son found responsible was important to my family."
Asked if Monday's award would help her heal, Juditha Brown said: "Life goes on. Every day is a step of healing."
